diagnostic_evidence.quote: These results are consistent with those established in \cite{HL2020} and \cite{HJL2021}.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction says the examples demonstrate sharpness of the convergence rates. The paper only proves upper bounds |u-u_h| <= C h^Gamma (Theorems main theorem ex1 and ex1 CLT). No lower bound, matching counterexample, or optimality argument for any rate appears. The only supporting remark is that the 1/6 and alpha-stable rates agree with earlier papers. The rate Gamma also comes from balancing worst-case terms in a Krylov-type argument, which is not evidence of optimality.

failure_location.quote: Concrete examples are provided to illustrate our results and demonstrate the sharpness of the convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the sharpness claim and describe the rates as upper bounds, or add a rigorous lower-bound or optimality argument for a specific example.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised sharpness of the rates is unsupported. The formal upper-bound results are not affected.
issues.title: Claimed demonstration of sharpness of the rates is never established
issues.why_classification: The formal theorems survive, but an advertised mathematical property must be withdrawn or newly proved, which is more than a purely local wording fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau

issues.failure_explanation: The convolution translates (x,y,z) by the same vector (e,e,e) with e in R^d. It therefore smooths only along the diagonal directions and not in each variable separately. Example (d=1): v=min(|x-y|,1) is bounded and Lipschitz and satisfies v(t,x-e,y-e,z-e)=v(t,x,y,z), so v^eps=v is not C^infty. Hence the claim v^eps in C_b^infty and the bounds ||d_t^i D^j v^eps|| <= 2CK eps^{1-2i-j} fail for derivatives such as D_{xy}, D_y^2, D_{yz}, D_{xz}, D_x^3 and d_t D_z. In the main proof u^eps and u_h^eps are claimed to satisfy exactly these bounds, so the bounds feeding E_1 and E_2 are not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take zeta in C^infty(R x R^{3d}) with independent shifts (e_1,e_2,e_3) in x, y, z. The PIDE is translation invariant, so supersolution and Lipschitz arguments carry over, with only the constants (e.g. 2C eps, K_zeta) changing.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit error functions E_1 and E_2, and all rates built from them, rest on derivative estimates for a mollification that is not smooth in the stated variables.
issues.title: Mollifier shifts x,y,z by the same e in R^d, so v^eps is not smooth in R^{3d} and the derivative bounds fail
issues.why_classification: A local change of the mollifier definition restores all estimates, with rates and the structure of the argument unchanged. Only the numerical constants change.

issues.failure_explanation: u_h is piecewise constant in t and jumps at grid points. For example u_h(h^-,.)=phi, whereas u_h(h,.)=E[phi(x+h^{1/2}X,...)] differs from phi. So (C1), which states time regularity C_0|t-t'|^{1/2} with no h^{1/2} term, is false. The proven Lemma uh_regularity (ii) carries an extra additive h^{1/2}. The proof of the lower bound nevertheless uses ||u_h-u_h^eps|| <= 2C_0 eps (time shifts tau in [0,eps^2] can cross a grid point), which needs the h^{1/2} term. Within the same display the derivative bounds do include (eps+h^{1/2}), so the displayed bounds are inconsistent. The comparison data and the stated constants 2C_0 h^{1/2} and 4C_0 eps in Theorem main theorem (i) are therefore not what the argument yields.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State (C1) with the additive h^{1/2} (as in Lemma uh_regularity (ii)). Replace 2C_0 eps by 2C_0 eps + C_0 h^{1/2} in ||u_h-u_h^eps||, and adjust the constants in the lower bound of Theorem main theorem and in the lower bound of Theorem main theorem CLT.
issues.overall_effect: The lower-bound estimate u-u_h <= 2C_0 h^{1/2} + 4C_0 eps + E_1 holds only with an extra O(C_0 h^{1/2}) term. Rates are unaffected, since h^{1/2} <= h^gamma.
issues.title: Mollification error of u_h ignores the h^{1/2} time-jump term from Lemma uh_regularity (ii); (C1) is false as stated
issues.why_classification: Only a constant (an extra C_0 h^{1/2}) changes, which is absorbed by existing h^{1/2} terms. No new argument is needed and all rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: With q_1=3/2 the proof bounds |Delta_x omega|^{q_1} <= min(2||D_x omega||, ||D_xz omega|| h^{1/alpha}|Z|)^{q_1} by (2||D_x omega||)^{q_1-delta}(||D_xz omega|| h^{1/alpha}|Z|)^delta. This inequality min(a,b)^q <= a^{q-delta} b^delta holds only for delta <= q. For delta > q it is false (take a=1, b small: b^q > b^delta). Assumption (v) allows delta up to alpha < 2, and the interval (3alpha/4 v 1, alpha) contains values above 3/2 whenever alpha > 3/2. For those delta the exponent (3-2delta)/3 is negative and the bound is unjustified. A valid argument needs delta replaced by min(delta, 3/2), which changes the exponent h^{(4delta-3alpha)/(6alpha)}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict delta to (3alpha/4 v 1, alpha ^ 3/2] in the Lemma, in Assumption (v) and in the rate formulas, or equivalently replace delta by min(delta, 3/2) throughout using M^{3/2} <= (M^delta)^{3/(2 delta)}. Recompute Gamma accordingly, so that for alpha > 3/2 the first term becomes (2-alpha)/(4 alpha).
issues.overall_effect: For alpha > 3/2 and delta in (3/2, alpha), the consistency bound, the explicit E_1 and E_2, and the rate Gamma are unsupported. In particular the claimed supremum 1/(4 alpha+6) of the first rate term is not reached. The correct rate for such alpha uses delta=3/2, i.e. (2-alpha)/(4 alpha).
issues.title: Interpolation estimate in R_21 invalid for delta > 3/2; negative exponent in Lemma consistency
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained restriction or truncation of delta with recomputation of exponents. The method is unchanged and a comparable positive rate survives, but the advertised rate for alpha > 3/2 degrades.
